- tests/test_update_workflows_manifest_verify.py | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test writes an executable `#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 1\n` script to `tmp_path / "bin" / "mktemp"` and expects the verify step to fail with `reason=workdir_unavailable` and no `gh` calls. When `tmp_path` resolves to a noexec mount, the fake `mktemp` cannot be invoked, so the system falls back to the real `mktemp -d` (which succeeds) and the verify step proceeds to call `gh`; the `assert calls == []` assertion then fails with `calls` containing the two `api` calls, producing a rejection reason other than `workdir_unavailable`.
  WHY: The editor's earlier sandbox run on 2026-10-09 had `/tmp` mounted noexec and hit exactly this failure mode (entry[4] in pr_all_comments_context.txt: "I ran the new test anyway by stubbing `yaml`, … putting a dummy `jq` on PATH and using a temp directory under `$HOME`"). The same failure reproduces in any runner whose `tmp_path_factory` base is noexec.
  Line or code reference: test_workdir_failure_rejects_before_any_gh_call (the test added by the last autofix run), and the @needs_tools marker that gates it
  Additional suggested fix: Extend @needs_tools (or add a sibling marker) to probe tmp_path executable mount: write a `#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n` script to tmp_path/bin and skip if `[ -x ]` is false. Alternatively, set TMPDIR via tmp_path_factory to a path known to be executable for this module's tests. Estimated lines changed: 4.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
- Requirement: "If the plan cannot be read, use the provisional names and behaviour in this issue and record that assumption in a code comment and the PR body." (issue #6960, Scope section)

The PR-body half is not: the inlined PR description is just "Automated implementation. Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/6960 Refs #6902" and discloses neither the plan-read failure nor the provisional names. Five consecutive autofix editor summaries (entry[1]-entry[5] in pr_all_comments_context.txt) acknowledge and defer the gap because the PR description is GitHub metadata outside the editor's workspace, so a human with `gh pr edit` access needs to add the assumption text before this PR is merged.
